_comment: Historical FIFA World Cup base rates used to GROUND and CALIBRATE the knockout model (engine/tournament.py, engine/mpp.py). These are the 'chiffres des coupes du monde' the knockout sim is checked against — not inputs the model blindly copies, but targets the Elo/Poisson + extra-time machinery must reproduce within tolerance (see engine/history.py:calibration_check).
sources: Wikipedia — List of FIFA World Cup penalty shoot-outs
Opta Analyst — World Cup Penalty Shootouts: The Facts
ESPN / Wikipedia — 2026 FIFA World Cup format & knockout stage

knockout_base_rates._comment: Empirical knockout-stage rates across World Cup history. Used as calibration targets; tolerances are deliberately wide (small samples, format changes).
knockout_base_rates.share_to_extra_time_note: ~1 in 4 World Cup knockout ties are level after 90' and go to extra time. The Poisson+Dixon-Coles draw probability for an even tie sits ~0.25-0.27, so the model reproduces this without a special rule.
knockout_base_rates.share_to_penalties_note: ~1 in 8 knockout ties are still level after 120' and decided on penalties (2022 was an outlier high at 5 of 16 = 0.31).
knockout_base_rates.goals_per_game_note: World Cup knockout games (R16 onward, historically) average ~2.4-2.6 goals over 90'. The 2026 format adds a Round of 32 with eight winner-vs-third ties that are MORE lopsided than any historic knockout round, so the simulation's 90' average runs a touch hotter (~2.7) — expected, not a miscalibration. Calibration tolerance is wide accordingly.
knockout_base_rates.favourite_advance_rate_note: The higher-rated side advances ~2/3 of the time over a knockout tie (incl. ET/pens) — knockouts are materially more random than a single result suggests, which is why outright/stage probabilities must come from a full simulation, never from chaining single-match favourites.

penalty_shootout._comment: Shootouts are close to a coin-flip; skill leans the odds only slightly. The engine models P(stronger side wins the shootout) = 0.5 + SHOOTOUT_SKILL_LEAN * (win_expectancy - 0.5).
penalty_shootout.skill_lean_note: 0.20 means the stronger side in a 60/40 (by 90' win-expectancy) tie wins the shootout only ~52% of the time — deliberately close to a coin-flip, matching the historical record that shootouts barely track favouritism.
